oil.summary: Crude sold off hard on Monday, with WTI down 3.95% to $85.06 and Brent off 4.17% to $91.84, extending a bruising month that has seen both benchmarks shed roughly 16%. Refined products led the rout — heating oil cratered 6.68% and RBOB fell 4.93%. The move is counterintuitive against a backdrop of acute supply-side stress: Ukraine claims drone strikes have disabled more than 55% of Russian refining capacity, Iran's output has plunged below domestic needs amid the ongoing US-Israel conflict, Iran is maintaining its Hormuz blockade, the UN reports 25 seafarers killed in Hormuz waters, and Houthi fighters have advanced to within 100 km of Aden, threatening Saudi export routes. Market pricing appears to be front-running a demand-destruction narrative and potential ceasefire diplomacy, amplified by Trump's warning to Zelensky to halt refinery strikes. Options markets now price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2027 meeting, suggesting the street expects the demand outlook to remain weak.
drivers: Sharp broad sell-off across crude and products despite multiple active supply disruption risks (Hormuz blockade, 55%+ Russian refining capacity offline, Houthi threat to Saudi exports)
Trump pressure on Zelensky to cease drone attacks on Russian refineries introduces potential diplomatic de-escalation signal
CME OPEC Watch pricing 77% probability of a production cut at the May 2027 meeting, reflecting deteriorating demand outlook

gas.summary: Henry Hub slipped 3.37% on the day to $3.121/MMBtu, though the month-on-month reading remains essentially flat at +0.16%, suggesting the intraday move is primarily weather-driven rather than a structural repricing. The key dynamic today is a divergence between the US and European markets: US LNG flows hit a reported all-time high, boosting export volumes and tightening domestic balances modestly, yet milder-than-expected European weather forecasts caused Amsterdam benchmark prices to slump, pulling sentiment across the complex. That said, Europe's structural position remains precarious — storage sites have already surrendered 10% of summer injections entering the heating season at multi-decade lows. Russia launched 116 attacks on Ukrainian energy and gas infrastructure over the past week, adding a persistent geopolitical risk premium to the European supply outlook. The TAPI pipeline remains a watch item, with Turkmenistan targeting completion of a key section by year-end.
drivers: US LNG exports at record highs are absorbing domestic production, yet milder European weather forecasts weighed on global gas sentiment and pushed Henry Hub lower
Europe enters deep heating season at multi-decade low storage levels, having already drawn down 10% of summer injections — structural tightness remains
Russia's 116 attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure last week sustain elevated disruption risk for European supply routes

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs eased a modest 0.88% to $83.265/EUA, holding the bulk of a 2.90% monthly gain. Power and carbon headline flow today was thin on sector-specific catalysts. The most notable directional data point is China, where thermal power generation fell year-on-year for the fourth consecutive month in October, with year-to-date thermal output down 0.1%, driven by wind and solar surging — a structural bearish signal for coal demand. On the geopolitical side, Iran ruled out UN inspections of damaged nuclear sites until hostilities end, and Bahrain reported intercepting Iranian attacks, keeping Middle East risk elevated but without a direct near-term read-through to European carbon pricing. The Iran-related Britannica headlines in the feed carry no actionable market content. Overall, the EUA market is consolidating recent gains with limited fresh catalysts today.
drivers: China's thermal power output fell year-on-year for the fourth straight month in October as wind and solar generation surged, pressuring global coal demand
EUA prices holding monthly gains of ~2.90% but seeing modest profit-taking today amid thin sector-specific catalysts
Ongoing Iran conflict — nuclear site inspections blocked, Bahrain intercepting Iranian strikes — sustains broad energy risk premium but lacks direct power/carbon price catalyst today
